p.src: Now among the twenty or thirty local rogues and loafers outside the Suanzao Gate, two were their leaders: one was Zhang San, nicknamed “Street-Crossing Rat,” and the other Li Si, nicknamed “Green-Grass Snake.” With these two at their head, they came to meet him. Zhishen happened to be walking toward the cesspit and saw that the whole band stood motionless beside it. In unison they said, “We have come especially to congratulate you, Master.” Zhishen said, “Since you are all neighbors from hereabouts, come sit inside the residence.” Zhang San and Li Si fell to their knees and refused to rise, hoping the monk would come help them up, whereupon they meant to seize him. Seeing this, Zhishen had already grown suspicious. “These scoundrels look thoroughly disreputable, and they will not come any nearer. Can they mean to throw me down? The curs have come to pluck a tiger’s whiskers! I shall go forward and let the curs see what my hands and feet can do.” Zhishen strode boldly toward the group. Zhang San and Li Si said, “We humble brothers have come especially to pay our respects to you, Master.” Even as they spoke, they moved forward, one lunging for his left leg and the other for his right. Before they could close with him, Zhishen’s right foot was already in the air; with a thump, he kicked Li Si headfirst into the cesspit. Just as Zhang San was about to flee, Zhishen’s left foot flew up, and both rogues ended up struggling in the cesspit. The twenty or thirty loafers behind them stared in stunned amazement and all made ready to run. Zhishen shouted, “If one man runs, one man goes in; if two run, two go in.” None of the rogues dared move. Presently Zhang San and Li Si poked their heads up from the cesspit. The pit proved seemingly bottomless. The two men stood in it smeared all over with stinking filth, their hair crawling with maggots, and cried, “Have mercy on us, Master!” Zhishen roared, “You rogues, hurry and haul those bastards out, and I shall spare the lot of you.” They all pitched in to rescue them and supported them over to the gourd trellis, but the stench and filth made it impossible to approach. Zhishen laughed heartily. “You witless creatures! Go wash yourselves in the garden pond, then come back, and I shall speak with all of you.”

p.src: After the two rogues had washed themselves, the others took off some garments and gave them clothes to wear. Zhishen called, “All of you, come into the residence, sit down, and talk.” Zhishen seated himself first in the central place, pointed at the men, and said, “You damned wretches, do not try to deceive me. What manner of damned men are you? How dare you come here and make sport of me!” Zhang San, Li Si, and all their companions knelt together and said, “Our families have lived here for generations, and we make our living solely by gambling for money. This vegetable garden is our livelihood. The Daxiangguo Temple has tried several times, even spending money, to deal with us, but could do nothing. From what monastery have you come, Master, to be so formidable? We have never seen you at the Xiangguo Temple before. From this day forward, we willingly place ourselves at your service.” Zhishen said, “I was formerly a garrison major under the Old Commandant of Yan’an Prefecture in Guanxi. But because I killed too many men, I willingly entered the religious life and have come here from Mount Wutai. My family name in the secular world was Lu, and my religious name is Zhishen. Never mind a mere twenty or thirty fellows like you—even amid an army of thousands, I would dare carve my way in and out again.” The rogues repeatedly murmured their assent, bowed their thanks, and departed. Zhishen returned to his room in the residence, put everything in order, and lay down to rest. The next day, the rogues pooled some money, bought ten jars of wine, and brought a pig to feast Zhishen. They prepared everything in the residence, invited Lu Zhishen to sit in the central place, and seated the twenty or thirty rogues in rows on either side to drink. Zhishen said, “Why should all of you waste your money on me?” They replied, “We are fortunate that today we have you here, Master, to stand as patron to us all.” Zhishen was delighted. When they were half drunk, some sang, some told stories, some clapped their hands, and some laughed. While they were making merry, they suddenly heard crows cawing outside the gate. Some of the men clicked their teeth, and all chanted, “May the red tongue rise to heaven and the white tongue sink into the earth.” Zhishen said, “What damned nonsense are you making now?” They answered, “When crows cry, we fear there will be quarrels and slander.” Zhishen said, “Where did you get such an idea?” The gardener laughed and said, “A new crow’s nest has appeared in the green poplar by the corner of the wall, and every day they make a racket until nightfall.” The men said, “Let us take a ladder up and tear down the nest. That will settle it.” Several said, “We will go at once.” Zhishen too, borne along by the wine, went outside with them to look, and sure enough there was a crow’s nest in the green poplar. The men said, “Let us climb up with a ladder and pull it down, and then our ears will have some peace.” Li Si said, “I shall shimmy up for you. There is no need for a ladder.” Zhishen studied the tree for a moment, walked up to it, removed his monk’s robe, reached down with his right hand and bent his body over, gripped the upper trunk with his left, then gave one heave from the waist and tore the green poplar up by the roots. When the rogues saw this, they all fell to the ground in worship, crying, “Master, you are no ordinary mortal, but a true arhat in the flesh! Without the strength of ten million catties, how could anyone uproot it?” Zhishen said, “What is so damned remarkable about that? Come tomorrow and watch me demonstrate arms and weapons.” That evening the rogues each went their separate ways.

p.src: From the next day onward, the twenty or thirty loafers were utterly submissive whenever they saw Zhishen. Every day they brought wine and meat to feast him and watched him demonstrate martial arts and boxing. After several days, Zhishen thought, “I have eaten a great deal of their food and wine every day. Today I shall prepare something and return their hospitality.” He sent the gardener into the city to buy several kinds of fruit, purchase two or three shoulder-loads of wine, and slaughter a pig and a sheep. It was then the end of the third month, and the weather was quite hot. Zhishen said, “The weather is hot.” He ordered the gardener to spread reed mats beneath a green pagoda tree and invited all the rogues to sit in a circle. Wine was poured into great bowls and meat cut into large chunks. When everyone had eaten his fill, fruit was brought out, and the wine-drinking grew ever merrier. The rogues said, “These past few days we have seen you display your strength, Master, but we have not seen you wield a weapon. If only you would let us watch once!” Zhishen said, “Well spoken.” He went into his room and brought out his solid-iron monk’s staff, five feet from end to end and weighing sixty-two catties. Everyone was astonished at the sight and said, “Without the strength of arms as mighty as a water buffalo’s, how could anyone wield it?” Zhishen took it in hand and at once sent it whistling through the air, every movement of his whole body perfectly coordinated. At the sight, everyone cheered as one.

Hearing this, Zhishen checked his hands and looked over. Beside a broken section of the wall stood an officer.
How was he attired? Behold:

p.src: Upon his head he wore a cornered cap of blue gauze; behind it, two white-jade rings adorned his hair at the temples. He wore a light green silk battle robe patterned with roundels, and about his waist was a double-ended silver belt with a tortoiseshell design. On his feet was a pair of court-style black boots with melon-shaped toes, and in his hand he held a folding paper fan from Western Sichuan.

p.src: The officer had a leopard-like head, round eyes, a swallow’s jaw, and tiger whiskers. He stood about eight feet tall and was thirty-four or thirty-five years of age. He said, “This master is truly extraordinary. How skillfully he wields his weapon!” The rogues said, “If this instructor applauds him, he must indeed be good.” Zhishen asked, “Who is that officer?” They replied, “That gentleman is Instructor Lin, the arms instructor of the eight hundred thousand Imperial Guards. His name is Lin Chong.” Zhishen said, “Why not invite him over so that we may meet?” Instructor Lin promptly leapt through the breach in the wall. The two met beneath the locust tree and sat down together. Instructor Lin asked, “Brother, where are you from? What is your religious name?” Zhishen replied, “I am none other than Lu Da of the Western Passes. Only because I killed too many men did I willingly become a monk. In my youth I also visited the Eastern Capital and knew your honored father, Commissioner Lin.” Lin Chong was delighted and at once swore brotherhood with Zhishen, taking him as his elder brother. Zhishen asked, “What brings you here today, Instructor?” Lin Chong answered, “Just now I came with my humble wife to the neighboring Temple of the Sacred Peak to fulfill a vow with incense. When I heard the staff being wielded, the display caught my eye. I told our maid Jin’er to accompany my wife into the temple to burn incense while I waited here. I never expected to meet you, Brother.” Zhishen said, “I have only just arrived here and knew no one, but these good fellows have kept me company every day; and now that you too have not disdained me and have become my sworn brother, nothing could be better.” He then told the temple attendant to bring more wine for his guest. They had drunk only three cups when the maid Jin’er appeared at the breach in the wall, flustered and flushed, crying, “Master, do not sit there any longer! The mistress is quarreling with someone in the temple.” Lin Chong hurriedly asked, “Where?” Jin’er replied, “At the foot of the Five Sacred Peaks Tower. She ran into a shameless scoundrel who barred her way and refuses to let her go.” Lin Chong said in alarm, “I shall come back to see you, Brother. Forgive me, forgive me.”

p.src: Taking leave of Zhishen, Lin Chong hastily leapt through the breach and hurried with Jin’er into the Temple of the Sacred Peak. When he rushed to the Five Sacred Peaks Tower, he saw several men standing by the railing, holding pellet bows, blowpipes, and birdlime poles; and on the narrow stairway a young man stood alone with his back turned, blocking Lin Chong’s wife and saying, “Go upstairs and let me speak with you.” Lin Chong’s wife flushed and said, “In a peaceful and orderly world, what justice permits you to molest an honest man’s wife?” Lin Chong rushed forward, seized the young man by the shoulder, jerked him around, and shouted, “What punishment do you deserve for molesting an honest man’s wife?” Just as he was about to strike, he recognized the young man as Young Master Gao, the adopted son of his own commander, Grand Marshal Gao. It turned out that Gao Qiu, newly risen to power, had no son of his own and no one to support him. He had therefore adopted into his household the son of his uncle, Gao Sanlang. Though they were actually cousins, Gao Qiu made him his adopted son. For that reason, Grand Marshal Gao cherished him. In the Eastern Capital, the scoundrel relied upon that power to tyrannize others and made a particular sport of violating other men’s wives and daughters. p.src: Lin Chong led his wife and their maid Jin’er out beneath the covered walkway. Just then Zhishen strode into the temple carrying his iron monk’s staff and leading twenty or thirty of the down-and-outs. Seeing him, Lin Chong called, “Where are you going, Brother?” Zhishen replied, “I have come to help you fight.” Lin Chong said, “It turned out to be the young master of my own commander, Grand Marshal Gao. He did not recognize my wife and behaved discourteously for a moment. I had intended to give the scoundrel a sound beating, but that would have reflected poorly on the Grand Marshal. As the old saying goes, ‘It is not officials one fears, but those who have direct authority over one.’ Since I have the misfortune to draw my pay from him, I shall let the fellow off this once.” Zhishen said, “You may fear the Grand Marshal because he commands you, but why the devil should I fear him? If I ever encounter that wretched bird, I shall first let him taste three hundred blows from my monk’s staff.” Seeing that Zhishen was drunk, Lin Chong said, “What you say is right, Brother. But the others persuaded me for the moment, so I have provisionally spared him.” Zhishen said, “If ever anything happens, just summon me and I shall go with you.” Seeing that Zhishen was drunk, the rogues supported him and said, “Master, let us go for now. We can meet again tomorrow.” Holding his monk’s staff, Zhishen said, “Sister-in-law, please do not take offense or laugh at me. Brother, we shall meet again tomorrow.” Zhishen took his leave and departed with the rogues. Lin Chong led his wife and Jin’er homeward, but his heart remained oppressed and joyless.

p.src: Now Gao Yanei, after leading a band of idlers to see Lin Chong's wife only to be driven off by Lin Chong, had become utterly infatuated. He returned to the residence dejected and miserable, brooding over his frustration. Two or three days passed. The many idlers all came to wait upon him, but when they saw Yanei distraught and beside himself, they eventually dispersed. Among them was a hanger-on named Fu An, nicknamed Dry Bird-Head. He understood what Gao Yanei wanted and went alone to wait upon him at the residence. Finding Yanei sitting idly in his study, Fu An stepped forward and said, “Your face has grown thin of late, Yanei, and you seem to take little pleasure in anything. Something must be troubling you.” Gao Yanei said, “How did you know?” Fu An replied, “I can hit upon it with a single guess.” Yanei said, “Then guess what is making me unhappy.” Fu An said, “Yanei is pining for the one whose name is made of two ‘wood’ characters. How is that for a guess?” Yanei laughed and said, “You have guessed correctly, but I have no way of getting her.” Fu An said, “What is so difficult about that? You are afraid that Lin Chong is a formidable man and dare not wrong him—but that need not trouble you. He now serves under the Marshal's command and receives a handsome salary. How would he dare incur the Marshal's displeasure? At the least, he could be tattooed and exiled; at the worst, his life could be taken. I have thought of a plan that will enable Yanei to possess her.” Hearing this, Gao Yanei said, “I have seen many beautiful women, yet for some reason she alone has captured my heart. I am bewitched by her and can find no joy in anything. If you have some clever scheme and can procure her for me, I shall reward you richly.” Fu An said, “Among your retainers is your trusted confidant, Constable Lu Qian. He is Lin Chong's closest friend. Tomorrow Yanei should conceal yourself in a secluded upper chamber at Constable Lu's house and have wine and food laid out. Then tell Lu Qian to invite Lin Chong out for a drink and have him go straight to a private upper room at Fan Tower to drink. I shall then go to his house and tell Lin Chong's wife, ‘Your husband, the Instructor, was drinking with Lu Qian when he was suddenly seized by some grave ailment and collapsed upstairs. He says you must hurry there to see him!’ Thus I shall trick her into coming upstairs. Women are fickle by nature. When she sees such a handsome and dashing gentleman as Yanei, and you coax her with a few sweet words besides, she cannot help but consent. What does Yanei think of my plan?” Gao Yanei cried his approval: “An excellent plan! Send someone to summon Constable Lu this very evening and give him his instructions.” As it happened, Constable Lu's home stood in the alley next to Grand Marshal Gao's residence. The next day, after they had discussed the scheme, Constable Lu reluctantly agreed, for there was nothing else he could do; intent only on pleasing the young Yanei, he cast aside the bonds of friendship.

u.src: Now Gao Yanei, after leading a band of idlers to see Lin Chong's wife only to be driven off by Lin Chong, had become utterly infatuated. He returned to the residence dejected and miserable, brooding over his frustration.
Two or three days passed. The many idlers all came to wait upon him, but when they saw Yanei distraught and beside himself, they eventually dispersed.
Among them was a hanger-on named Fu An, nicknamed Dry Bird-Head. He understood what Gao Yanei wanted and went alone to wait upon him at the residence.
Finding Yanei sitting idly in his study, Fu An stepped forward and said, “Your face has grown thin of late, Yanei, and you seem to take little pleasure in anything. Something must be troubling you.”
Gao Yanei said, “How did you know?”
Fu An replied, “I can hit upon it with a single guess.”
Yanei said, “Then guess what is making me unhappy.”
Fu An said, “Yanei is pining for the one whose name is made of two ‘wood’ characters. How is that for a guess?”
Yanei laughed and said, “You have guessed correctly, but I have no way of getting her.”
Fu An said, “What is so difficult about that?
You are afraid that Lin Chong is a formidable man and dare not wrong him—but that need not trouble you.
He now serves under the Marshal's command and receives a handsome salary. How would he dare incur the Marshal's displeasure?
At the least, he could be tattooed and exiled; at the worst, his life could be taken.
I have thought of a plan that will enable Yanei to possess her.”
Hearing this, Gao Yanei said, “I have seen many beautiful women, yet for some reason she alone has captured my heart. I am bewitched by her and can find no joy in anything.
If you have some clever scheme and can procure her for me, I shall reward you richly.”

Fu An said, “Among your retainers is your trusted confidant, Constable Lu Qian. He is Lin Chong's closest friend. Tomorrow Yanei should conceal yourself in a secluded upper chamber at Constable Lu's house and have wine and food laid out. Then tell Lu Qian to invite Lin Chong out for a drink and have him go straight to a private upper room at Fan Tower to drink.

I shall then go to his house and tell Lin Chong's wife, ‘Your husband, the Instructor, was drinking with Lu Qian when he was suddenly seized by some grave ailment and collapsed upstairs. He says you must hurry there to see him!’
Thus I shall trick her into coming upstairs.
Women are fickle by nature. When she sees such a handsome and dashing gentleman as Yanei, and you coax her with a few sweet words besides, she cannot help but consent.
What does Yanei think of my plan?”
Gao Yanei cried his approval: “An excellent plan!
Send someone to summon Constable Lu this very evening and give him his instructions.”
As it happened, Constable Lu's home stood in the alley next to Grand Marshal Gao's residence.
The next day, after they had discussed the scheme, Constable Lu reluctantly agreed, for there was nothing else he could do;
intent only on pleasing the young Yanei, he cast aside the bonds of friendship.

p.src: Now Lin Chong had remained deeply troubled for days and had no desire to go out into the streets. Around the hour of the Snake, he heard someone at the door call, “Is the Instructor at home?” When Lin Chong came out to look, he saw that it was Constable Lu and hurriedly said, “What brings you here, Brother Lu?” Lu Qian replied, “I came especially to see you, brother. Why have I not seen you in the streets these past few days?” Lin Chong said, “I have been troubled at heart and have not gone out.” Lu Qian said, “Come with me, brother, and let us drink a few cups to dispel your gloom.” Lin Chong said, “Sit a while and have some tea first.” After the two had drunk their tea, they rose to leave. Constable Lu said, “Sister-in-law, I am taking our elder brother to my home for a few cups.” Lin Chong's wife hurried to the cloth curtain and called, “Husband, do not drink too much, and come home early.” Lin Chong and Lu Qian went out through the door and strolled idly along the street for a while. Constable Lu said, “Brother, let us not go to my home. We may as well have a couple of cups here at Fan Tower.” The two went up into Fan Tower, secured a private room, and summoned a waiter, ordering two flasks of the finest wine and rare fruits to accompany it. As they chatted about this and that, Lin Chong heaved a sigh. Constable Lu asked, “Why do you sigh, brother?” Lin Chong said, “You do not understand, worthy brother… What use is it for a man to possess all these skills if he finds no enlightened lord, but must languish beneath petty men and endure such filthy humiliation!” Constable Lu said, “There may be several instructors in the Imperial Guards, but which of them can equal your skill, brother? The Marshal also treats you well. Who, then, has caused you such vexation?” Lin Chong related to Constable Lu the whole affair involving Gao Yanei the other day. Constable Lu said, “Yanei surely did not recognize your wife. Do not be angry, brother. Let us simply drink.” After Lin Chong had drunk eight or nine cups, he felt the need to relieve himself. Rising, he said, “I shall go wash my hands and return.”

p.src: Lin Chong came downstairs, left the tavern, and went into a little alley to the east to relieve himself. As he turned back out of the alley, he saw the maid Jin'er calling, “Master, I've had such trouble finding you—and here you are!” Lin Chong asked in alarm, “What has happened?” Jin'er said, “Less than half an hour after you went out with Officer Lu, a man came rushing to the house in great haste and told my mistress, ‘I am Officer Lu's neighbor. Your husband, the Arms Instructor, was drinking with Lu Qian when suddenly his breath failed him and he collapsed. You must come quickly and see him.’ When my mistress heard this, she hurriedly asked Granny Wang next door to watch the house, then she and I followed the man to a house in an alley before the Grand Commandant's residence. When we went upstairs, we saw wine and food laid out on a table, but you were nowhere to be seen. Just as we were about to go downstairs, the young man who had harassed my mistress at the Temple of the Great Peak the other day appeared and said, ‘Sit a while, madam. Your husband will be here presently.’ I rushed downstairs in fright, and then heard my mistress upstairs crying murder; so I searched everywhere for you, but could not find you. Then I happened upon Doctor Zhang, the medicine seller, who said, ‘As I passed the Fan Tower, I saw the Instructor go inside to drink with another man.’ That is why I came running here. Please hurry, master!” At these words Lin Chong started in shock. Without even waiting for Jin'er, he raced to Officer Lu's house, taking three steps at a stride. He charged up the steep stairs, only to find the upper door barred, and heard his wife cry, “In a peaceful and orderly world, how dare you shut an honest man's wife in here?” Then he heard Young Master Gao say, “Madam, have pity and save me. Even a heart of iron or stone could be moved by such entreaties.” Standing on the stairs, Lin Chong called, “Wife, open the door!” Recognizing her husband's voice, the woman hastened straight to the door. Young Master Gao took fright, wrenched open an upper window, jumped over the wall, and fled. Lin Chong went upstairs but could not find Young Master Gao. He asked his wife, “That brute did not defile you, did he?” She replied, “No.” Lin Chong smashed Officer Lu's house to pieces. He took his wife downstairs, and when they went outside, they saw that all the neighbors on either side had shut their doors. The maid Jin'er met them, and the three returned home together. Lin Chong took a sharp wrist-cutting knife and went straight to the Fan Tower to seek Officer Lu, but he too had vanished. He returned and waited before Lu's door all night, but Lu never came home, so Lin Chong went back to his own house. His wife urged him, “He did not succeed in deceiving me, after all. You must not act recklessly.” Lin Chong said, “That accursed beast Lu Qian! I treated you like my own brother, and you too would deceive me! If I fail to run into Young Master Gao, I shall at least see to Lu's face and head!” His wife pleaded with him bitterly and would by no means let him leave the house. Officer Lu hid in the Grand Commandant's residence and dared not return home. Lin Chong waited for three days in succession without once seeing him. Those before the residence saw the grim look on Lin Chong's face, and none dared question him.

p.src: At mealtime on the fourth day, Lu Zhishen went straight to Lin Chong's house to visit him and asked, “Instructor, why have I not seen you these past several days?” Lin Chong replied, “I have been slightly occupied and have not had the chance to call on you, elder brother. Since you have honored my humble home with a visit, I ought to offer you a few simple cups, but unfortunately I cannot prepare them properly at such short notice. What say you to strolling through the streets with me and buying a cup or two in town?” Zhishen said, “Excellent.” The two went into the streets together and drank all day, arranging to meet again the next day. From then on, Lin Chong went drinking in town with Zhishen every day and gradually let the matter drop. Indeed:

p.src: When Officer Lu and Fu'an saw the old chief steward come to inquire after the illness, they conferred and said, “There is only this one way.” They waited until the old steward had finished his visit and come out, then drew him aside to a secluded place and said, “If the young master is to recover, the only way is to inform the Grand Commandant and have Lin Chong put to death. Then his wife can be united with the young master, and the illness will be cured. If this is not done, the young master will certainly lose his life.” The old steward said, “That is easily done. I shall report it to the Grand Commandant this very evening.” The two said, “We already have a plan. We shall await your reply.” That evening the old steward went to see the Grand Commandant and said, “The young master suffers from no ordinary ailment; his malady is Lin Chong's wife.” Gao Qiu asked, “When did he see the man's wife?” The steward reported, “It was on the twenty-eighth of last month, at the Temple of the Great Peak. More than a month has now passed.” He then related in full detail the plan devised by Officer Lu. Gao Qiu said, “I see—yet merely because of the man's wife, how can we bring harm upon him? Still, when I think on it, if I spare one man, Lin Chong, I must surely sacrifice my son's life. What, then, is to be done?” The steward said, “Officer Lu and Fu'an have a scheme.” Gao Qiu said, “If that is so, summon the two men here to confer.” The old steward immediately summoned Lu Qian and Fu'an into the hall, where they bowed in greeting. Gao Qiu asked, “What plan do you two have concerning my young master? If you restore my son to health, I shall see that you are both well rewarded.” Officer Lu stepped forward and reported, “Your Excellency, there is but one way: we must do thus and thus.” After hearing him out, Gao Qiu applauded and said, “An excellent plan! You two shall carry it out for me tomorrow.” Of this, no more need be said.

p.src: When Lin Chong had examined it, he started in amazement and blurted out, “What a magnificent sword! How much do you want for it?” The man said, “I ask three thousand strings of cash, but the firm price is two thousand.” Lin Chong said, “It is indeed worth two thousand strings, but it has found no master who appreciates it. If you will take one thousand, I shall buy it.” The man said, “I urgently need money. If you truly want it, I will yield five hundred strings and take fifteen hundred, firm.” Lin Chong said, “One thousand only. At that price, I will buy it at once.” The man sighed. “Selling gold for the price of scrap iron! Very well, very well—but do not short me by a single cash.” Lin Chong said, “Come home with me, and I will pay you there.” Then he turned to Zhishen and said, “Elder Brother, wait awhile in the teahouse. I shall return directly.” Zhishen said, “I shall go back for now. We will meet again tomorrow.”

p.src: After parting from Zhishen, Lin Chong led the sword seller home, paid him, and asked, “Where did you obtain this sword?” The man said, “It was handed down by my ancestors. My family has fallen into poverty, so I had no choice but to bring it out and sell it.” Lin Chong asked, “Who was your ancestor?” The man replied, “To name him would only bring terrible shame upon me!” Lin Chong questioned him no further. The man took the money and went his way. Lin Chong turned the sword over and over, examining it for some time, then exclaimed in admiration, “This truly is a splendid sword! Grand Marshal Gao has a precious sword in his residence, but for no good reason he refuses to let anyone see it. Several times I asked to borrow it for a look, yet he would never bring it out. Now that I too have bought a fine sword, I shall take my time comparing it with his.” That evening Lin Chong could not put the sword down and examined it all night; at bedtime he hung it upon the wall. Before dawn had even broken, he went to look at it again.

p.src: At about the hour of the Snake the next day, he heard two attendants calling at his gate: “Instructor Lin, the Grand Marshal commands you: since you have bought a fine sword, you are to bring it for comparison. The Grand Marshal is waiting especially for you at his residence.” Hearing this, Lin Chong said, “Some busybody must have told him.” The two attendants hurried Lin Chong into his clothes. Taking the sword, he followed them. Lin Chong said, “I do not recognize either of you from the residence.” The two men replied, “We entered his service only recently.” Before long they reached the residence, entered, and came to the front hall. Lin Chong stopped, but the two men said, “The Grand Marshal is seated in the rear hall within.” They passed around a screen into the rear hall, but the Grand Marshal was nowhere to be seen. Lin Chong stopped again. The men said, “The Grand Marshal is waiting for you farther inside and ordered us to conduct you in, Instructor.” After passing through another two or three gates, they reached a place enclosed on every side by green railings.
